panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Clinical photograph of the primary lesion on the left thenar eminence in a patient whose biopsy was diagnostic of clear cell acanthoma; the solitary erythematous papule/nodule is a recognized clinical manifestation of CCA. B: Low-power H&E of the diagnostic shave biopsy showing psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia composed of pale-staining keratinocytes, the classic histologic pattern of clear cell acanthoma attributed in the caption and text to CCA. C: Higher-power H&E demonstrating the sharp demarcation between the pale-celled epidermal tumor and adjacent normal epidermis, a characteristic histologic feature of clear cell acanthoma explicitly captioned in this CCA case.
panels.attribution_text: Melson et al. Clear Cell Acanthoma with Malignant Cytologic Features: A Case Report and Review of the Literature.. Dermatopathology (Basel, Switzerland) 2022. doi:10.3390/dermatopathology9040041. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: (A) Clinical image of the initial left thenar eminence lesion, prior to shave biopsy. (B) Low power examination of the initial shave biopsy specimen revealed an epidermal tumor exhibiting psoriasiform hyperplasia composed of pale staining cells (H&E, 20×) with (C) an abrupt transition to the adjacent normal epidermis at one lateral edge (H&E, 100×).
in_text_mentions: A 78-year-old male with prior history of immune thrombocytopenia and multiple nonmelanoma skin cancers presented to dermatology clinic with a new growth on the thenar eminence of the left palm (Figure 1A) measuring 1.0 cm × 0.8 cm. He reported it had been present for several weeks and was occasionally painful. It persisted after treatment with liquid nitrogen. At his next visit, a tangential biopsy was performed. Histopathology showed marked epidermal hyperplasia with areas of well-demarcated pallor and mild spongiosis consistent with CCA (Figure 1B,C).

in_text_mentions: A 73-year-old woman presented with less than a 1-year history of an erythematous, well-delimited and shiny lesion on her left buttock, near the gluteal fold (Fig. 1). Dermoscopic examination showed dotted vessels arranged in a linear pattern involving the entire lesion. These vascular findings are also called metaphorically a ‘string of pearls’ pattern. Another vascular pattern observed on the periphery of the lesion is that of branched vessels with rounded endings. panels.rationale: Excised gross specimen of the patient's lesion on a surgical drape with rulers, matching the caption describing the raised verruciform and mamillated cutaneous neoformation; article title identifies it as a giant clear cell acanthoma. Real patient tissue showing a specific manifestation of the configured disease; giant size makes it a recognized less-common (variant) presentation.
panels.attribution_text: Cuomo et al. Human Papillomavirus-Associated Giant Clear Cell Acanthoma and Squamous Cell Carcinoma: A Rare Case Report and Literature Review.. Journal of clinical medicine 2024. doi:10.3390/jcm13092482. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Raised verruciform and mamillated cutaneous neoformation lesion measuring 12 cm in length, 6 cm in width, and 5 cm in height.
in_text_mentions: Clinically, the lesion was observed as a raised verruciform and mamillated cutaneous neoformation, measuring 12 cm in length, 6 cm in width, and 5 cm in height (Figure 1, Figure 2 and Figure 3). It was characterised by a broad base of implantation and exhibited a taut elastic consistency. Additionally, two minor satellite neoformations were identified at the 3 o’clock and 11 o’clock positions relative to the primary lesion, each measuring 1.5 cm by 1.5 cm and displaying similar morphological features.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Panel A shows H&E stained epithelial tumor exhibiting characteristic morphological features of Clear Cell Acanthoma, specifically psoriasiform hyperplasia and pale keratinocytes, which was the basis for the diagnosis in the case. B: Panel B shows H&E stained superficial dermis containing melanophages, a feature mentioned in the article supporting the final diagnosis of Clear Cell Acanthoma with melanophages.
panels.attribution_text: de Oliveira et al. Clear Cell Acanthoma with Melanophages Simulating a Spitz Nevus.. Dermatology practical & conceptual 2021. doi:10.5826/dpc.1103a89. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: (A) Epithelial tumor showing psoriasiform hyperplasia, parakeratosis, and pale cytoplasm of keratinocytes (H&E, ×40). (B) Some melanophages were present in the superficial dermis (H&E, ×100).
in_text_mentions: le measuring 3 × 4 mm located on her right shoulder (Figure 1A). The dermoscopic findings were equivocal, revealing brown globules with regular distribution and a brown blotch at the periphery (Figure 1B). The first hypothesis was that of a Spitz Nevus, and excision was indicated. Histological examination (H&E stain) revealed an epithelial tumor characterized by psoriasiform hyperplasia, parakeratosis, and large keratinocytes with pale cytoplasm. Some melanophages were evident at the level of the superficial dermis (Figure 2). Thus, a clear cell acanthoma (CCA) with melanophages was diagnosed.
